**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – critical revenue protection; no documented path from signup → first class → habit formation. Missing: goal-setting capture, coach assignment logic, welcome touchpoints, baseline assessments.
- **Member Checkins** – no scheduled retention intervention; at-risk members slip away undetected. Missing: frequency triggers, conversation framework, escalation rules.

- **Member data privacy & GDPR** – compliance gap; no documented handling of personal data, consent, deletion requests, breach protocol.

- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – no systematic quality control; inconsistent coaching standards across studio.

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Start with your revenue reality, not your wish list** — Audit what your coaches are *actually* selling right now (1-on-1s, small groups, class passes, nutrition coaching?). List the price each generates. This stops you creating a menu that doesn't match your business model.

• **Build two separate, brutally honest documents** — Coaches' version: lists what they can genuinely deliver, pricing authority they have, upsell sequences, commission structure. Members' version: stripped of jargon, shows outcome ("tone and strength in 12 weeks"), not features. No coach should be explaining their own offerings differently than the menu states.

• **Anchor pricing to your actual class capacity and coach hours** — If you run 25 classes/week with 15 capacity each, that's your throughput ceiling. Price group classes to hit your revenue target even at 70% capacity. Price 1-on-1s 3-4x the hourly equivalent of group rates so it's actually attractive for coaches to sell and you to deliver.

• **Create a decision tree coaches physically use** — "New member asking about options?" → "Budget under £50/month? → Group classes. £50-150? → Hybrid package. Over £150? → Personal coaching." This stops paralysis and ensures consistent pitch.

• **Test one offering this week with 3-5 members** — Propose the menu to early adopters, watch what questions they ask about pricing/inclusions. You'll spot gaps before printing or publishing anything.
